title: Capability-based fallback ranking
description: Candidate tools are described by the capabilities they provide, and the request lists the capabilities it needs. The selector ranks candidates by capability coverage and picks the highest-ranked healthy one. This keeps fallbacks functionally correct instead of merely available. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers matching required capabilities against candidate sets.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: {"need": ["search", "filter"]}, 2: {"need": ["search", "filter", "rank"]}, 3: {"need": ["search", "filter", "rank", "dedup"]}}
need = set(CFG[LEVEL]["need"])
tools = {"t1": ({"search", "filter"}, True), "t2": ({"search"}, True), "t3": ({"search", "filter", "rank", "dedup"}, False), "t4": ({"search", "filter", "rank"}, True)}
cands = [(name, len(caps & need)) for name, (caps, healthy) in tools.items() if healthy and need <= caps]
cands.sort(key=lambda x: -x[1])
print("need:", sorted(need), "| ranked:", cands, "| chosen:", cands[0][0] if cands else "NONE")
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Degradation ladder
description: Fallbacks are ordered from full-fidelity to minimal in a degradation ladder. The selector walks down the ladder until it finds a working rung, so users get the best quality currently achievable. Each rung documents what is lost relative to the preferred tool. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers walking an ordered ladder of decreasing fidelity.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 2, 2: 3, 3: 4}
DOWN_UNTIL = CFG[LEVEL]
ladder = [("full-llm", True), ("small-llm", True), ("template", True), ("cached", True), ("static", True)]
for i in range(DOWN_UNTIL):
    ladder[i] = (ladder[i][0], False)  # top rungs down
chosen = next((name for name, up in ladder if up), None)
lost = [name for name, up in ladder if not up]
print("down rungs:", lost, "| serving from:", chosen)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Health-checked routing
description: Each candidate tool receives periodic health probes, and the routing table marks tools healthy or unhealthy. The selector only routes to healthy tools and re-checks on a schedule, so failover happens without human intervention. Probe failures trigger deeper diagnostics before a tool is marked down. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers periodic health probes per candidate.

title: Cost-quality tradeoff fallback
description: When the preferred tool is unavailable, the selector scores alternatives by quality per unit cost and picks the best value. A slightly lower-quality but dramatically cheaper tool often beats a premium fallback. Scores combine measured quality, latency, and price. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers scoring candidates by quality per cost.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: {"budget": 10}, 2: {"budget": 5}, 3: {"budget": 2}}
BUDGET = CFG[LEVEL]["budget"]
cands = [("premium", 0.95, 8.0), ("standard", 0.85, 2.0), ("economy", 0.70, 0.5)]
ok = [(n, q / c) for n, q, c in cands if c <= BUDGET]
ok.sort(key=lambda x: -x[1])
print("budget:", BUDGET, "| value-ranked:", [(n, round(v, 3)) for n, v in ok], "| chosen:", ok[0][0] if ok else "NONE")
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Cached-result fallback
description: If no live tool can serve the request, the selector serves the last known-good cached result, labeled with its age. Stale data with a staleness warning beats no data for many read workloads. Cache entries carry TTLs and provenance so consumers can judge trust. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers serving last-known-good results with staleness labels.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: {"age": 30}, 2: {"age": 300}, 3: {"age": 3600}}
AGE = CFG[LEVEL]["age"]
cache = {"q1": {"result": "42", "age_s": AGE, "ttl_s": 600}}
entry = cache["q1"]
fresh = "FRESH" if entry["age_s"] <= entry["ttl_s"] else "STALE"
print("serving:", entry["result"], "| age: %ds" % entry["age_s"], "| status:", fresh, "| provenance: cache")
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.
